definitions.explanation: To scrape or rake with nails or claws, often causing marks or injury. Used for both humans and animals.

examples.japanese: {猫|ねこ}に{腕|うで}を{引|ひ}っ{掻|か}かれた。
examples.english: I got scratched on the arm by the cat.

examples.japanese: {蚊|か}に{刺|さ}されたところを{引|ひ}っ{掻|か}いてしまった。
examples.english: I scratched the spot where I was bitten by a mosquito.

examples.japanese: {爪|つめ}で{壁|かべ}を{引|ひ}っ{掻|か}くような{音|おと}がした。
examples.english: There was a sound like scratching the wall with nails.

notes:
CONJUGATION:
・{引|ひ}っ{掻|か}く → {引|ひ}っ{掻|か}かない (negative)
・{引|ひ}っ{掻|か}く → {引|ひ}っ{掻|か}いて (te-form)
・{引|ひ}っ{掻|か}く → {引|ひ}っ{掻|か}いた (past)

FORMATION:
Compound verb: {引|ひ}く (to pull) + {掻|か}く (to scratch)

The {引|ひ}っ- prefix intensifies the scratching action.

COLLOCATIONS:
・{爪|つめ}で{引|ひ}っ{掻|か}く - to scratch with nails
・{猫|ねこ}に{引|ひ}っ{掻|か}かれる - to be scratched by a cat
・{傷|きず}を{引|ひ}っ{掻|か}く - to scratch a wound

KANJI NOTE:
{掻|か}く is often written in hiragana as かく due to the complexity of the kanji {掻|か}.
